program: NSF Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER), NSF 22-586
direction: CISE / Information and Intelligent Systems (IIS): machine learning for ecological monitoring
title: CAREER: Reliable machine learning for automated biodiversity monitoring under distribution shift
background: Camera traps, passive acoustic recorders and drone imagery now generate far more ecological observations than experts can label, and machine-learning classifiers have become the default way to turn these streams into species occurrence and abundance data. Yet models trained at one set of sites, seasons or sensor types degrade sharply when deployed elsewhere, and the errors are not random: rare, cryptic and nocturnal species are systematically under-detected, which biases the very population trends that conservation decisions rely on. Ecologists have few tools to know when a model's output can be trusted at a new site, or how its errors propagate into downstream estimates such as occupancy or trend models. This CAREER project will develop machine-learning methods that detect and adapt to distribution shift in ecological sensor data, quantify prediction uncertainty in a form that ecological models can ingest, and prioritise the scarce expert labels where they most improve population estimates. The integrated education plan will train undergraduate and graduate students from ecology and computer science to build and critically evaluate such tools together.
challenges: Detecting and adapting to distribution shift across sites, seasons and sensors when labelled data from the new deployment are scarce or absent
Class imbalance and long-tailed species distributions: rare and cryptic species are the most ecologically important and the most often missed
Propagating classifier uncertainty into ecological inference (occupancy, abundance, trend models) instead of treating predicted labels as ground truth
Allocating limited expert annotation effort where it most improves the ecological estimate rather than classifier accuracy alone
Designing education activities that genuinely integrate with the research rather than running alongside it
sponsor: U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE)

budget.note: CAREER awards must total a minimum of $400,000 over 5 years ($500,000 for BIO, ENG and OPP). The minimum is a floor, not a cap; this task is placed in CISE, so the $400,000 / 60-month minimum applies.

eligibility: The PI must hold a tenure-track or tenure-track-equivalent assistant professor position (or equivalent untenured title) at a US institution of higher education, with an appointment of at least 50% that includes both research and educational responsibilities. An eligible PI may submit only one CAREER proposal per annual competition. No co-PIs are permitted.
requirements: Present a single integrated plan of research and education, not a research plan with a separate outreach add-on
Describe the proposed research: specific objectives, methods and procedures, and expected significance of the results (preliminary supporting data where appropriate)
Describe the proposed educational activities, including plans to evaluate their impact
Describe how the research and educational activities are integrated with each other
Describe other broader impacts, beyond the education plan, that will result from the project
constraints: Total award of at least $400,000 over 5 years (CISE)
Project Description is limited to 15 pages
